title: Spinning current hall sensor with residual offset calibration signal
relevant_features: Spinning-current Hall readout with chopping/demodulation; residual-offset calibration via lengthened phases, dual-frequency chopping, inverted spin direction, zero-bias phases
overlap_with_supplied_work: Directly overlaps CC-2's core mechanism: rotating bias through Hall terminal sequences with polarity chopping and demodulation to cancel offset (project 02 8-state phase table, a2 chopper reversal)
potential_distinction: IF distinguishable at all, only via the specific external-discrete implementation (external floating current loop, CMOS mux network, GaN 2DEG plate, fusion in-vessel context) - the generic spinning+chopping method itself is squarely claimed here and in a large family
notes: Active (anticipated expiration 2029-04-09). Related family incl. US9110121B2 and US8154281B2 (seen in search results, not individually fetched). Dense corporate patent thicket around spinning-current readout

title: Hall sensor with interleaved and/or sliding averaged/summed spinning phases
relevant_features: M spinning-current Hall sensors (X/Y/Z channels) with N spinning phases interleaved across channels; multiplexed readout; sliding averaging to cut inter-channel delay/jitter
overlap_with_supplied_work: Closest patent art to CC-3's synchronized multi-axis spinning: project 03 plans one Pico 2 fanning shared a0/a1/a2/EN to three boards so all axes spin in phase with zero inter-axis skew
potential_distinction: Project 03's scheme is simultaneous phase-locked spinning of three independent analog channels (not interleaved/multiplexed single-path readout); discrete boards + shared clock fan-out vs monolithic IC - distinction is conditional and narrow
notes: Active (expires 2038-08-24). Shows Infineon already patents multi-channel spinning coordination; any CC-3 claim must be drafted around this family

title: High temperature hall sensor for magnetic position sensing
assignee_or_authors: Ohio State Innovation Foundation (inv. Heremans, Myers, Gao, Yang)
relevant_features: Group III-nitride (AlGaN/GaN and AlN/GaN 2DEG) Hall sensors operating at >=300-350 C; current injection + Hall voltage processing; temperature compensation via sheet resistance
overlap_with_supplied_work: Overlaps the device premise of CC-1/CC-2: GaN 2DEG Hall element used for magnetic sensing in high-temperature/harsh environments
potential_distinction: Application abandoned 2016 (prior art still effective as publication). Claims were position/rotation sensing with permanent magnet, not plasma-facing field diagnostics; fusion in-vessel deployment and UHV packaging are outside its claims
notes: Abandoned (failure to respond to office action, 2016); remains citable prior art as a published application; whether and how it qualifies under 35 USC 102 in any analysis is a counsel determination. Demonstrates GaN-2DEG-Hall-in-harsh-environment was published patent literature by 2014

title: Method and apparatus for steady-state magnetic measurement of poloidal magnetic field near a tokamak plasma
assignee_or_authors: US Department of Energy (inv. Robert D. Woolley)
relevant_features: Steady-state poloidal-field measurement near a tokamak plasma: pickup coils + periodic current-pulse/strain-gauge mechanism; self-calibrating electronics correcting integrator drift
overlap_with_supplied_work: Overlaps CC-4's problem statement exactly (drift-free steady-state in-vessel field measurement with a hybrid of inductive and non-inductive channels) though with strain, not Hall, as the absolute channel
potential_distinction: Expired (fee-related, 2016) - freedom-relevant only as prior art. Hall-vs-strain absolute channel, Kalman-type estimation, and stellarator context differ; but it anticipates the architecture-level idea of drift-corrected hybrid in-vessel magnetics
notes: DOE-assigned: also evidence that national-lab fusion magnetics concepts get patented. CC-4 claims would need to be much narrower than 'hybrid drift-corrected fusion magnetics'

title: Method of auto calibrating a magnetic field sensor for drift and structure therefor
assignee_or_authors: Semiconductor Components Industries LLC (orig. AMI Semiconductor Belgium; inv. Charlier, Laulanet, Badaroglu)
relevant_features: Sensitivity-drift auto-calibration using measurement phases with a varying reference magnetic field; isolates external field, calibration field, and offset contributions; 4-electrode bias/sense switching
overlap_with_supplied_work: Overlaps CC-5's logic of separating a known reference field from the unknown measured field to fix sensitivity in situ
potential_distinction: Active (expires 2029). Uses an on-board generated reference coil field; CC-5's reference is the machine's own confinement-coil vacuum field computed from coil currents at a surveyed pose - a facility-level, computation-anchored reference, not an embedded coil. Distinction conditional
notes: Together with PA-P07/EP1789813A1-type art, shows dense coverage of 'known reference field calibrates sensor in place'

title: Magnetic field sensor and method for calibrating the same
relevant_features: Calibration coil energized with known current; measured field change yields sensitivity; automatic calibration independent of temperature

potential_distinction: Expired (2022, fee-related). Bench Helmholtz calibration is unpatentable standard practice; only the specific coil-only-shot + surveyed-pose + computed-vacuum-field anchor chain could even conditionally be argued as a new combination
notes: Confirms the generic 'known coil current as calibration reference' concept has been patented and has now expired into the public domain
